method: Nonexclusive qualitative notes for all 54 discordant dialogues, based on each pair’s successful final Q/A, largest losing rank deterioration and repetition profile; full histories inspected for selected mechanisms. Tags describe observations across runs, not adjudicated causes. Images inspected for 106,343,1399,1406 and all six universal failures.

56.note: MMR asks time of day (night) and hits at r1; vanilla loops on objects and light location.

69.note: Vanilla reaches logs and zoo; alternatives accumulate vegetation/deer details. Existence of deer not image-verified here.

106.note: Probe imports cat from questions while answers confirm sink/mirror colours. Image has no cat; later simulator denial also contradicts it. Removing cat partly repairs retrieval.

161.note: Vanilla hits with yellow and green; probe first obtains green and yellow, then invents a second moving train. CPU colour-order-only replay crosses top-10.

233.note: MMR succeeds with crouching; vanilla adds a second blue-shirted person after a gender question. No image verification of the second person.

234.note: Vanilla repeats generic questions after an unsure answer; MMR/probe reach field/fence details. Probe also contains a malformed question, so success is not evidence of uniformly good questions.

297.note: S2 ends with black office/black cat and loses bookcase emphasis; vanilla reaches brown bookcase and chandelier. Some black attributes spread across objects.

332.note: Vanilla asks how many and gets four; MMR loops on zebra without recovering the count.

343.note: Probe adds sandwich and then pizza from colour-question premises; simulator later says unsure about sandwich. Target image contains small food bowls, no sandwich/pizza. Removing sandwich partly repairs retrieval.

454.note: MMR obtains eating and succeeds; vanilla foregrounds a sky background and loops on generic objects.

504.note: Vanilla succeeds immediately from yellow sink; MMR pursues beige flooring/toilet/tub and pink towels, with the sink dropped from final focus.

508.note: Vanilla gets Wimbledon immediately; probe accumulates common clothing/court attributes and repeats court colour.

621.note: Vanilla describes white pants; MMR gets white shorts and succeeds. S2 success also imports white headband from a question premise. Probe later gets banner detail. Do not attribute every win to cleaner grounding.

670.note: Vanilla succeeds after an unsure breed answer and rewording; probe adds colours and loses late-in-the-day emphasis. A hit here does not establish informative questioning.

701.note: S2/probe reach yellow building; vanilla adds a stone and crowd and repeats traffic-light questions.

722.note: All variants eventually use red kite; probe asks it first. Vanilla changes two children into a female/male/group description while pursuing background questions.

742.note: Vanilla succeeds with clothing (shorts/black shirt); MMR repeatedly retrieves pink-kite information and later introduces khaki pants.

767.note: Vanilla repeats fire-hydrant answers; probe gets naked when asked shirt colour. S2 gets skinny to a colour question and succeeds, a semantically odd but retrieval-helpful answer.

858.note: S2 calls clock tower metal after a material question, while vanilla uses stone and reaches lamp details. Material correctness not image-verified.

894.note: Early blue-jacket answer hurts S2/probe; vanilla eventually finds gray hat and fence. S2 has a question referring to image 6 rather than a grounded target attribute.

955.note: Probe eventually gets cloudy lighting; vanilla deteriorates after black shirt and repeats generic questions.

975.note: Vanilla changes big wave to small from simulator answer; S2/probe reach cloudy weather. Initial caption and answer conflict; no automatic rule establishes which is correct.

1004.note: Vanilla reaches multicoloured clothing at r10; S2 calls four people men, probe repeats black skis. Clothing specificity differs.

1078.note: S2 succeeds with detailed street-corner surroundings; probe reaches street signs; vanilla repeats stop sign and suffers from changing long rewrites.

1098.note: Vanilla eventually changes green/white bus to blue/white and hits; MMR preserves initial bus colours and adds traffic-light details. Image not inspected for colour truth.

1109.note: Probe describes a white acrylic bathtub while saying bathtub not visible; vanilla reaches water heater and sink.

1111.note: MMR obtains object inventory then yellow wall; vanilla focuses on appliance colours and materials.

1169.note: S2/probe eventually get black desk; vanilla changes computers into two laptops on a wooden desk and repeats laptop.

1288.note: Vanilla succeeds from giraffes eating from a wall; S2 uses leaves and repeats location. Image not checked, so do not assume either object answer is correct.

1301.note: Vanilla enumerates many doughnut varieties and table/tablecloth details; S2 reaches metal container and brown doughnuts. More descriptive text is not necessarily better retrieval.

1399.note: Target visually is a double-decker bus. MMR revises initial trolley caption and hits r6; vanilla retains trolley while adding buses/vans/ferris wheel.

1406.note: Target visually shows traffic signals, not flags. Vanilla uses the correction and hits; S2 collapses query toward clear sky/no flags. Preserving the initial description blindly would be wrong.

1411.note: Vanilla succeeds after repeating wood windowsill; probe adds many colours and a gray countertop. This is a counterexample to assuming repetition always causes failure.

1466.note: Vanilla collapses group of motorcycles into a black motorcycle and drifts; S2 later includes surrounding mountains.

1510.note: Vanilla includes crowd and black shirt; MMR begins with ambiguous behind him, then focuses on common court/racket/ball details.

1540.note: Vanilla succeeds with large green open field; S2 substitutes savanna and loops, although both descriptions could be valid.

1542.note: Probe introduces fireplace from television-colour question; removing only fireplace clause improves rank 70 to 19. Vanilla succeeds before that path.

1543.note: Probe reaches beige walls; vanilla repeats colours and adds wood vanity material to an already complex bathroom description.

1577.note: S2 reaches wood and bathtub; vanilla accumulates fixtures and white tiled surfaces. Logs alone cannot isolate the decisive detail.

1579.note: MMR adds directing traffic and replaces red truck with car; vanilla remains near top-10 while repeating traffic light. Final successful step is a generic repeat, not a novel question.

1598.note: Vanilla invents another blue-shirted man while handling socks; probe reaches black hair and succeeds. MMR also ends with another tennis ball.

1639.note: MMR succeeds from laptop immediately. Vanilla later changes standing people into a woman holding a laptop and adds another laptop; S2 eventually reaches typing.

1640.note: Vanilla succeeds after malformed question unexpectedly elicits blue cutting board; alternatives stay on stainless-steel cabinets/fridge. Win is not clean evidence of question quality.

1676.note: Vanilla has people holding bikes and hits; S2 rewrites them as riding bikes and adds cloudy weather/red signal.

1713.note: MMR gets Chicago Cubs and probe Wrigley Field; vanilla adds white shorts, ball colour and catcher-mitt details.

1731.note: Vanilla eventually gets Jack Russell; S2 adds hat, MMR repeats species/object questions. Hat correctness not verified.

1732.note: MMR turns one player into two, one mid-air, after a qualified likely jump-serve answer; vanilla gets blond hair and hits.

1788.note: Vanilla identifies living room and lamp; MMR adds cabinets and repeats wall colours.

1840.note: Probe finds Air India; vanilla stays with white trucks/planes. Airline identity is a concrete differentiator.

1862.note: Vanilla accumulates orange house/building and stop sign; variants reach car/traffic-light features. MMR final hit follows unsure answer, so question informativeness is ambiguous.

1894.note: Vanilla includes without a fireplace after denial and rank deteriorates. Probe corrects absent television and gets red chair; S2/MMR reach seating colours. Removing fireplace-negation alone helps partly.

2003.note: Vanilla reaches blue dress; S2 focuses on hard court/white racket and MMR repeats court/object. Clothing description differs.

2029.note: S2 gets river early; vanilla/MMR repeat elephant and fail. Probe also fails, so the useful setting is not reliably selected.

2057.note: Vanilla succeeds after malformed candidate-image question elicits a broader scene description; probe adds orange stop sign. S2 repeats other object. No clean cause from outcome alone.
